key_insight: ShapeCond condenses time-series datasets by explicitly preserving local discriminative motifs (shapelets), producing a tiny synthetic training set that retains classification performance while being much faster to train on.
problem_solved: Standard dataset condensation methods are image-centric and miss time-series temporal structure, causing loss of local motifs (shapelets) that are critical for classification; ShapeCond addresses efficient, faithful condensation tailored to time series.
method: Extract or learn class-discriminative shapelets (local motifs) to identify what information must be retained from the original series.
Synthesize a small set of representative time-series exemplars via a shapelet-guided objective that aligns condensed examples with extracted motifs and class decision boundaries.
Optimize the condensed set with a fast, gradient-based procedure designed for time-series models, yielding strong accuracy vs compression trade-offs with low compute overhead.
impact: ShapeCond enables practitioners to drastically reduce dataset size for time-series classification without sacrificing accuracy, speeding up training, lowering storage and compute costs, and making model iteration and deployment more efficient.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: original time-series → shapelet extraction → shapelet-guided synthesis → condensed set → classifier
Overlay illustration: original series with highlighted shapelets and matching motifs in condensed exemplars
Bar/line chart: accuracy vs. condensation ratio comparing ShapeCond to baselines
Runtime and memory comparison: training time and storage savings (ShapeCond vs full dataset)
paper_title: ShapeCond: Fast Shapelet-Guided Dataset Condensation for Time Series Classification
paper_authors: Sijia Peng, Yun Xiong, Xi Chen, Yi Xie, Guanzhi Li
